title: Algorithm Problems: Part 2
refresher: A multi-step algorithm may track a **value** plus its **index**, or a count plus a total. State what remains true after each pass, and define empty **input** and tie behavior.

blocks.body: A multi-step algorithm may track a value plus its **index**, or a count plus a total. State what remains true after each pass, and define empty **input** and tie behavior. Coordinate multiple state values and **edge cases**.

blocks.title: Track best-so-far state
blocks.caption: Watch the best index update only when a better value appears.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.body: Best starts at index 0 because that is the first candidate.

steps.title: Compare index 1
steps.body: Nine is larger than four, so best moves to index 1.

steps.title: Compare index 2
steps.body: Seven is not larger than nine, so best stays put.

blocks.body: Part 2 problems often need two related facts at once. A largest-**value** search may keep an **index** because that index provides both the value and its location. An invariant is simply a sentence that remains true after each pass, such as: `best` points to the largest item examined so far.

blocks.caption: The first item initializes the candidate; each later item may replace its **index**.
Guard the empty case before choosing a first candidate.
blocks.wrong:
let best = 0;
return values[best]; // fails when empty

blocks.body: Trace `[4, 9, 7]`: best begins at zero, **index** one contains a larger **value** so best becomes one, and index two does not replace it. The invariant remains true after every comparison. Decide separately whether equal values should keep the first or last index.

blocks.title: Trace this carefully
blocks.body: Empty **input** has no first candidate, so guard it before reading **index** zero and choose an explicit contract.

choices: index zero is already the candidate
blocks.why: The first element was already used to initialize the best candidate.
The later equal **value** does not pass a strict greater-than test, so the first remains.

algo-p2-01.title: Sorted flag invariant
algo-p2-01.body: This algorithm keeps a flag that means no out-of-order pair has been found yet. Each pass compares a value with the value just before it.
algo-p2-01.notice: The loop starts after the first item because each comparison looks backward one position.
algo-p2-01.mistake: Do not compare a value with itself or start at a position with no previous neighbor.

algo-p2-02.title: Running totals
algo-p2-02.body: Running totals keep one ongoing total and record a snapshot after each addition. The saved collection grows after the current value is included.
algo-p2-02.notice: Add first, then store the new total for that position.
algo-p2-02.mistake: Do not reset the total each pass; only the snapshot changes each pass.

algo-p2-03.title: Nested matrix scan
algo-p2-03.body: A matrix count needs two loops: one to choose each row and one to inspect each value in that row. The counter changes only on a target match.
algo-p2-03.notice: The inner loop must be nested inside the row loop.
algo-p2-03.mistake: Do not increment once per row when the prompt asks for matching cells.

algo-p2-04.title: Two best values
algo-p2-04.body: Tracking the largest and second-largest distinct values means the variables depend on each other. When a new largest appears, the old largest has to move into second place.
algo-p2-04.notice: Update second before replacing largest with the new value.
algo-p2-04.mistake: Do not let a duplicate of the largest count as the second-largest distinct value.

algo-p2-05.title: First occurrences
algo-p2-05.body: This pattern preserves order by scanning left to right and adding a value only if it has not already been kept.
algo-p2-05.notice: The membership check happens before the append or add step.
algo-p2-05.mistake: Do not sort the values or use a plain set if the prompt asks to keep first-seen order.

algo-p2-06.title: Mirrored string positions
algo-p2-06.body: A palindrome check compares matching positions from the front and back. One mismatch is enough to change the answer flag.
algo-p2-06.notice: Only half the string needs direct comparisons.
algo-p2-06.mistake: Do not compare every character with the same final character.

algo-p2-07.title: Reset row-local state
algo-p2-07.body: A best-row algorithm has two levels of state: a row total that restarts for each row and a best value that survives across rows.
algo-p2-07.notice: Reset the row total inside the outer loop but before the inner loop.
algo-p2-07.mistake: Do not reset the best value for every row.

algo-p2-08.title: Separate kept values and zeros
algo-p2-08.body: Moving zeros to the end can be traced as two pieces of state: the kept nonzero values and the number of zeros seen so far.
algo-p2-08.notice: The scan preserves nonzero order first, then appends the counted zeros.
algo-p2-08.mistake: Do not append zeros immediately if the prompt wants them all at the end.
